story: Jordan, 20, a UCLA junior, came off his bike on Bruin Walk and broke his wrist: a non-displaced distal radius fracture. Ronald Reagan UCLA's emergency department X-rayed it, splinted it and gave a pain shot (real UCLA prices). He has a student health plan and works about 20 hours a week at a coffee shop, so his paychecks drop while he can't work: a week of sick pay, then light duty. About 120% of the poverty line. He got overcharged: the bill ignores his insurance, charges the wrist X-ray twice and prices the splint above UCLA's own posted charge. Once fixed, his share plus his cash follow-up care is over 10% of his income (take-home or gross), so UCLA's policy writes it off: $0.
